content:
There is a DSL highlights page for veil-2.0 at https://github.com/verse-lab/veil/tree/veil-2.0-preview

Compared to Ivy my question is if there is a difference in Veil 2.0 between the following or if they're equivalent as they are in Ivy?

1) let x <- pick T within an action vs. having an argument x of type T in the action

  • non-deterministic choice for x
    2) require p vs. if p

  • filter the valid executions using an if rather than a require

  • p rather than P, i.e no quantifiers

I think for the pairs you mentioned (pick, require, if), Veil 2.0 has essentially the same semantics as Ivy. Let me go through them one by one:

let x <- pick T within an action vs. having an argument x of type T in the action

These two are equivalent. Having x as an argument of the action is like hoisting the non-deterministic choice to the top level. At the verification condition level, both correspond to a quantifier over T (universal or existential depending on how non-determinism is interpreted), so the resulting VCs should be equivalent.

(One minor difference is where the quantifier appears: for pick, it may be nested inside the VC (e.g., within a branch of an if), whereas for action arguments it is typically prenexed.)

require p vs. if p

I assume require here has the same semantics as assume, e.g., when actions are invoked from the environment (such as in #check_invariants).

These two are not semantically equivalent, although the difference may not matter for verification. At the VC level, require p; ... (or assume p; ...) yields something like p -> ..., whereas if p then ... yields a VC of the form: if p then ... else (postcondition holds on the pre-state). In #check_invariants, since the invariant is assumed on the pre-state, the else branch holds trivially. So the VC reduces to if p then ... else True, which is equivalent to p -> ....

p rather than P, i.e. no quantifiers

Could you elaborate on this part?

Thank you for your clarifications!

On the last part: Ivy doesn't support forall in if statements, but it does support exists

Not sure if I fully understand your question, but the closest construct in Veil I'm aware of is the if x : p then e1 else e2 syntax. It is equivalent to: if (exists x, p) then (let x :| p; e1) else e2

Is this what you had in mind?

You fully answered my question. I was attempting to answer why I used p rather than P. The context here is that I'm considering how I translate/transcribe the Ivy models that we have, and for that I need precise semantics for some Veil DSL constructs, that correspond to coding conventions we use in Ivy, and that are not yet fully explained in the Veil DSL documentation
Yeah, that makes sense. The Veil DSL documentation is still incomplete at the moment. We're planning to improve it, but it will take some time. In the meantime, feel free to ask if anything comes up.
